market_context.summary: Friday 2026-10-30 closed hard risk-off on the surface and something stranger underneath: SPY -1.77% to 755.72, QQQ -3.47% to 690.49, IWM -1.65%, Intel -28.6% on a Q4 guide $1-2B below consensus. But GLD fell -3.47% to 355.78 — its lowest close in four months — alongside the Nasdaq, while TLT managed only +0.43%. Gold selling off as hard as tech with no duration bid is de-grossing and margin-covering, not a flight to safety. QQQ is now -9.5% off its 120-day high and below both its SMA20 and SMA50; SPY -3.3% and also below both; IWM is above its SMA20, so small caps outperformed on the way down, which is unusual. The one green sector was energy: XLE +1.91% to 70.02, a close 0.19% from its 120-day high, on Brent settling ~$117.64 (+13.6% for October) against a reported Iran-escalation premium explicitly timed to the Nov 3 midterms being past. The 10-year eased 5.05% to 4.98% with fed funds at 3.88%, a steep positive term premium, and unemployment ticked 4.1% to 4.2%. Index levels (SPX, NDX, VIX, DXY) and all futures could not be fetched today; the ETF proxies above are the numbers to trust.

catalyst.event: US midterm elections Tue Nov 3. Saxo Bank warned on Oct 29 that oil could be more volatile over the following couple of weeks because of the Israeli and US elections, and the reporting has traders fearing the Iran war — ongoing since February — intensifies after the vote; a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz was struck by explosive devices attached from a small boat, and Houthi militants claimed attacks on several Saudi sites on Oct 29. RTX interceptors and effectors are consumed in an air campaign and restocked at appropriated prices, unlike a decade-long platform backlog. RED TEAM CORRECTION: the stronger claim this report originally carried — that US airstrikes on Tehran could 'resume once the midterms are past' — is not what the cited sources say. Its only source is an aggregator (wisevoter) reporting that US forces 'may consider strikes against Iran following the November 3 midterm elections'; that page does not mention Tehran, names no original reporting and carries an AI-generated illustration. What is sourced is volatility expected around the vote, not a stated precondition for strikes. The idea is kept on its relative-strength and level evidence, not on that claim.
catalyst.action: Enter on the 196.50-201.50 zone, sized at 2.5%. Do NOT add size for the midterms. This is now the only new money in the Iran-escalation cluster — XLE and HII were moved to the watchlist, and that is a reduction of the exposure, not room made for more of the same trade.

recommendations.thesis: RTX is the defense prime whose revenue is consumed rather than ordered: an air-defense campaign burns Patriot and SM-series interceptors that are then restocked at appropriated prices, so escalation converts directly into orders instead of into a 10-year program. It is already outperforming into this — +7.99% over one month against SPY -1.08% and peer ITA +0.82% — while sitting 11.9% below a 120-day high of 226.88 that was set before the summer drawdown, so the target is a recovery to a level this stock has already traded at, not a new high.
recommendations.key_risk: The catalyst is binary and dated: if the midterms pass and no escalation follows, the whole Middle East premium across defense and energy unwinds together, and RTX gives back the 8% it made in October. Secondary: insiders sold $6.86M across 6 transactions in six months with zero open-market purchases, so there is no insider confirmation under this. Third, added by the red team and absent from the original write-up: the premium can unwind on diplomacy rather than on the midterms passing quietly — the same reporting has Qatari mediators returning to Tehran with US-Iran talks stalled, so a mediated de-escalation is a live path that takes the complex down with no dated event to trade around. Fourth: the sector has already repriced — Brent +13.6% in October, XLE at its 120-day high, LMT within 3% of its own — so RTX is the least repriced member of a repriced group, which is thinner edge than being early.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that I am buying a defense name after the sector has already repriced for war — LMT is within 3% of its high. Answered with the relative-strength data rather than assertion: RTX has beaten ITA by 7.17 points over 1 month, 6.99 over 3 months and 17.85 over 6 months, so the capital is rotating toward RTX within an already-hot sector, and its analyst revision direction is improving (bullish share 67.7%, +1.0 pt) with 4 beats in the last 4 quarters. The weaker point I cannot answer: I could not fetch the options-implied move (Yahoo options returned HTTP 401), so I cannot say whether a 13.4% target is inside or outside what the market prices.

recommendations.thesis: This is the one idea in todays report that does not depend on the Middle East. XLU is the sector that led the market over the past month, +9.45% against SPY -1.08%, while still sitting 6.85% below its 120-day high of 46.625 — the only leading sector with real distance left to a prior level, because healthcare (-1.7% off high) and staples (-1.1%) have already closed the gap. recommendations.key_risk: The catalyst is two-sided: a hot payroll print on Nov 6 pushes the 10-year back above 5% and utilities are the first sector sold. Second, this is the sector ETF for a thesis I rejected at the single-name level today — I dropped the VST bid because VST is lagging XLU by 10.4 points over a month on company-specific problems — so I am explicitly buying the basket and not the operators. Third, the target requires a 7.3% move, about 5.3 ATRs (3.30 against a 0.6282 ATR14) — inside the 6.0 ATR swing guide, but still a multi-week ask for a 1.45%-ATR sector fund. The original write-up put this at 'about 11 ATRs', which was wrong by a factor of two; corrected by the red team. Fourth, added by the red team: payrolls is not the only rate print inside the holding window. October CPI lands Nov 10, four sessions later, with no FOMC until Dec 9 to confirm either reading — so a soft NFP that re-rates the sector can be taken straight back by a hot CPI, and the idea has to survive two prints rather than the one it is framed around.

Both are long-duration equity proxies, so if the 10-year falls, XLU works and the IYR short bleeds — I am partly hedging myself. I am taking it anyway because XLU has a load-growth earnings driver that commercial real estate does not, and because the IYR short is 0.64 ATR from its stop and likely to resolve within days either way. But the reader should know the two positions overlap, and that is a real mark against this idea rather than something I can argue away.

data_quality_notes:
RESEARCH COMPLETE — notes.md carries a RESEARCH COMPLETE block at 06:34 ET and a FINAL COUNTS block at 06:37 that supersedes it with six candidates rather than five (ELAN was found after the first block was written, by screening insider activity across the fetched Nov 6 earnings list). A full falsification pass ran on all of them, so truncated is false. Research ran 06:00-06:37 ET.

PRICES ARE A CLOSED MARKET, NOT STALE DATA. Every equity and ETF mark in this report is the 2026-10-30 close (asof 2026-10-30T20:00Z), re-fetched at 06:34 ET Monday and unchanged, because US equities are shut. That is the freshest honest price available at this hour, not a failure to refresh. Bitcoin ($77,828) is live. SMA200 is unavailable on every name — only 120 days of history were pulled — so there are no 200-day reads anywhere in this report.

FLAG FOR THE RED TEAM — XLE AND HII WILL FAIL direction_consistency, AND IT IS AN ARTIFACT, NOT A BAD NUMBER. Both are position updates whose entire content is a protective stop on a position already deep in profit: XLE's stop moves 60.80 to 66.50 against a 63.90 fill now at 70.02 (+9.6%), and HII gets its first-ever stop at 288.00 against a 262.00 fill now at 316.88 (+20.9%). In both cases the stop therefore sits ABOVE the entry, which check_direction reads as 'downside is not below entry for a buy' and hard-fails. CLAUDE.md forbids the only fix that would clear it — a filled position may have its exits amended but never its entry, because it was bought at a price — so the entry stays at the fill and the check stays red. No prior report in this repo has ever shipped a stop on the profitable side of entry, so there is no precedent to follow. If phase 2d demotes these two to the watchlist, the result is that the single most valuable instruction in today's report — put a stop under a 21% gain that currently has none — is the thing that gets thrown away. Read the stop, not the verdict. Related: the reward-to-risk figures of 2.54 (XLE) and 2.99 (HII) are computed the way validate_report.py computes them, abs(target-entry)/abs(entry-stop), and they are not meaningful risk ratios — the 2.60 and 26.00 'risk' are locked-in gains, not money at risk.

WIN PROBABILITY ON THOSE SAME TWO IS ALSO MEASURED AGAINST THE WRONG BASELINE. The 1/(1+R:R) baseline is a random walk starting at the entry, and these two walks start at Friday's close, which is far nearer the target than the stop. Recomputed from current price: XLE's driftless baseline is 0.880 and the stated 0.72 is BELOW it; HII's is 0.558 against a stated 0.55, i.e. claiming no edge at all, just the geometry. Both will trip a '>20 points of claimed edge' check against the entry-based baseline. The four ideas entered at the market (RTX, XLU, SMMT, ELAN) have entries within 0.4% of last price, so for those the entry-based baseline is correct and the stated edges of +9.9, +4.8, +11.0 and +7.4 points stand as written.

WHY SIX IDEAS, AND WHY ALL SIX ARE SWING. Six is the honest count. Running the same two tests across every sector priced today gave one answer repeatedly: what is working is too close to its high to pay for an honest stop (XLP -1.1% off its high, XLV -1.7%, BJ -0.7%, DLTR -2.3%, XLE -0.2%, XOP -1.1%, OXY -1.5%, LMT -3.1%, EXEL -3.8%), and what is cheap is below both moving averages with heavy insider distribution and no datable catalyst (SLV -44.8% off its high, OKLO -67%, ARM -54.5%, WDC -54.2%, STX -43.7%). EQT, WMT, COST and XLP were each rejected for failing the floor at exactly that point. Nothing intraday cleared, because not a single live price could be fetched — the market is shut and every futures and index feed failed. Nothing long_term cleared: that lane lost its candidate when VST turned out to be lagging its own sector by 10.4 points on company-specific problems, and the sector ETF was bought instead rather than inventing a long-term single name.

RATIOS AND STOPS BOTH CLUSTER JUST ABOVE THEIR FLOORS, AND THAT DESERVES SUSPICION. Three of the four new ideas land at R:R 2.12 (RTX), 2.20 (XLU) and 2.22 (SMMT) against a 2.0 swing floor, and four of six stops land at 1.82, 2.07, 2.07 and 2.32 ATR against floors of 1.8 and 2.0 — inside the warn band below the 2.25/2.5 ATR level where this report's stop-outs have clustered. Every one of those figures was independently recomputed during synthesis from freshly fetched 120-day history and reproduced the research's numbers to the second decimal, so they are arithmetically sound; but clustering above a floor is the signature of levels fitted to clear a bar, and the reader should price that. Two points in mitigation: the research rejected WMT and COST specifically for computing to exactly 2.00, and it documented the order of operations on the one ratio that was mechanically improved (see below).

THE XLE STOP RAISE IMPROVED ITS OWN RATIO, WHICH IS THE MANOEUVRE THIS REPO WAS BURNED BY. Moving the stop 60.80 to 66.50 lifted reward-to-risk 2.13 to 2.54 without the trade getting one cent better — the KRE pattern named in CLAUDE.md.
